fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Perpetual synchronicity is a practice, not a lucky streak", "body": "Chance Garton opens by tying synchronicity directly to gratitude, describing how a defeatist train of thought the day before dissolved once he actually listed what he was grateful for, and the things he named promptly showed up in front of him. He argues a show like InnerVerse engenders this for listeners, because uplifting concepts tend to reappear in a listener's life in uplifting ways. Carla echoes it with her own month long experiment of asking eight questions at bedtime and on waking, including how her guidance system will guide her and how she will feel the support of the universe."}, {"title": "From rock climbing injury to biofield tuning", "body": "Chance traces his path into energy work. He started podcasting eight years ago before he was ready, chasing the question of how creative people at transformational arts festivals turned soul purpose into a livelihood. Nobody could hand him the secret. In 2020 he heard Eileen McCusick on Crowe 777 and the Higher Side Chats within a short span, bought a Sonic Slider tuning fork, and cleared a long term shoulder injury that turned out to be a back left heart chakra pattern of absorbing other people's negativity. He read her books rather than taking classes and has been tuning about four years."}, {"title": "All the gods resolving into one story", "body": "The heart of the conversation is Chance's research into language, symbolism and etymology, shared on his members podcast Inner World with cohost Dylan Socoscio. He argues world mythologies and religions run on the same tenets and only look different because a symbol carries many meanings. He cites Reverend Robert Taylor, who wrote The Devil's Pulpit and went to jail for showing the astro theology behind world religion, and Taylor's line that Christianity and paganism are as different as six and half a dozen. His target is what he calls the Disney vacation of mythology and pop culture gnosticism."}, {"title": "The big bang is the cosmic egg retold", "body": "Chance makes the case that scientific materialism repeats an ancient cosmology rather than replacing it. The ancients held matter itself to be eternal, with a mind awakening out of chaotic matter to shape it into a world, symbolized by Osiris set adrift by Typhon, by Noah in the ark, whose name he links to nous or mind, and by figures like Mithras and Phanes hatching from a cosmic egg. A singularity holding all matter that then explodes, he says, is that egg cracking. He also defends the divinity of matter and quotes Carl Jung's Seven Sermons to the Dead on the pleroma."}, {"title": "Worldview as self defense and symbolic literacy", "body": "The practical thread is that your life is a product of your worldview, so the twenty four hour news cycle of disease scares, shootings and political theater amounts to worldview warfare. Chance offers a blunt filter for whose ideas to accept, asking whether you would be bummed to trade lives with the person. He urges people back into mystery, imagining seeing the sun with no words for it, because explaining things explains them away. Symbolic literacy, he says, is a synchronicity enhancer and genuine psychic self defense, letting you read waking life the way you would interpret a dream."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: "Ancestral River" author Carla Adams invited me to hang for a live stream on her Youtube channel, and I'm looking forward to what gems we might unearth in this mind-meld.
